messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered - High 5xx rate for inference pool 'redwood-inference-usw3a' (us-west-3a). Current symptom: sudden spike in econnreset / 502s from runtime, NLB health check failures. Pager severity: P1. Notifying oncall-sre.

alice (oncall-sre): I’m on it. acked the pager and paging netops. First triage: are we seeing node flaps or network drops?

frank (pagerduty): frank: Pager history: 2143456788 - 2143456790, 1500 affected requests/min peak, 90% 5xx origin.

ben (eng-runtime): reprod: Rolling windows show KVCACHE stalls + repeated socket econnreset in the runtime logs. sample tail: ```
[2026-03-15T09:00:12Z] runtime: connection reset by peer while writing to socket
[2026-03-15T09:00:12Z] kvcache: miss spike, slot 42 flush timeout
```
I ran curl to the local health endpoint on a few pods: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/health` -> some nodes return 502, others 200. Node-level check shows high kernel retransmits.

carmen (netops): I'm seeing elevated ENI detach/re-attach counts in us-west-3a and NLB target unhealthy transitions. VPC flow logs show increased TCP RST from hypervisor side between instances and NLB subnets. Packet loss ~12% between host interfaces.

alice (oncall-sre): ok - sounds like a single AZ networking plane degradation. Can we quickly move critical traffic to cross-region fallback? What's our smart routing policy?

ben (eng-runtime): We have policy route->preferred: same-az variant -> same-region alt-az -> failover-region. Right now same-az is failing and alt-az pool in region is empty for this pool (we scale per-az). I can spin up fallback pool in us-west-3b but that may take ~4-6m for GPUs. Immediate quick mitigation: enable model-variant fallback to lower-memory quantized instance in other AZs + divert routing for new requests only. This will cut capacity but restore success rate.

david (oncall-eng): I'll trigger routing override. Command: `rctl routing override set --pool inference-usw3 --route failover:us-west-3b --reason "az3a net degradation"` and lower max concurrency. Applying now.

incident-bot: Routing override applied by david (oncall-eng). New requests will be diverted according to policy. Note: existing sticky sessions remain in place for 30s.

alice (oncall-sre): Carmen, can you validate that cross-AZ peering/NAT paths are healthy? We need to ensure failover target can accept traffic.

carmen (netops): peering looks ok, but NAT gateway in the same AZ has higher error rates. We're pushing egress to shared NAT in the region; that's healthy. I recommend steering away from affected ENIs (we can mark them degraded). I'm marking affected ENI set: eni-0a1b2c3d as degraded -> `aws ec2 create-tags --resources eni-0a1b2c3d --tags Key=redwood:net-state,Value=degraded` (this will signal autoscaler to avoid).

ben (eng-runtime): Runtime metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 18%->6% after routing override, latency slightly up for some requests. Logs show fewer econnresets. kvcache miss spike subsided.

eve (prod-support): Received ~27 customer error reports in last 10m. Most are timeouts/5xx. Opening a consolidated status note for CS and customers: will post preliminary impact and ETA for full mitigation. @gina FYI for customer comms.

gina (customer-success): Thanks. Please include list of affected tenants and note that cross-region fallback activated; some requests may be routed to lower-capacity variants and have higher latency.

alice (oncall-sre): Can we add an immediate temporary autoscale in other AZs for inference-usw3? Ben, coordinate with infra to bring up reserved instances or spin ephemeral nodes.

ben (eng-runtime): K8s cluster autoscaler is already queued for 6 extra pods in us-west-3b. Creating a faster path: `infra quick-provision --pool inference-usw3 --count 4 --type p4d-quant` -> provisioning started. ETA ~5m.

carmen (netops): Also seeing a higher-than-normal route churn in the AZ's route table updates from the cloud provider. Requesting a support case with AWS now. Opening case: `aws-support case: 1234567890 - AZ network plane degrad us-west-3a`

incident-bot: AWS support case 1234567890 opened by carmen (netops). Severity: Customer-impacting.

david (oncall-eng): Quick healthcheck commands for reference: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep inference-usw3a
kubectl logs -n inference <pod> --tail 100 | grep -E "EPIPE|connection reset" 
```
Used these to check which nodes to cordon. I'm cordoning the worst offenders to avoid new traffic: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-1-24.usw3a`

ben (eng-runtime): Cordoning done for 3 nodes. Draining one caused failing connections to redirect gracefully. No crashes observed during drain.

alice (oncall-sre): Summary so far: root cause appears to be AZ-level network degradation impacting ENI<>host connectivity causing NLB health-check failures and econnreset in runtime. Immediate mitigations: routing override -> divert new traffic to other AZs; mark ENIs degraded; cordon affected nodes; spin up 4 fallback nodes in us-west-3b. Impact: reduced errors from 18% -> 6%, partial customer impact remains for sticky sessions and inflight requests.

eve (prod-support): ETA updates: provisioning nodes ~5m, full traffic normalization ~15-20m once instances join and kvcache warms. Draft status for customers: "We are experiencing elevated error rates for some inference requests in US-WEST-3a. Traffic is being routed to fallback capacity; we expect normalization within 20 minutes. We're monitoring and will update in 10 minutes." Approve?

gina (customer-success): Approve, add note about customers with Dedicated deployments pinned to us-west-3a: we'll need to coordinate per-customer migration or emergency capacity reservations.

carmen (netops): AWS support says they see packet drops on the AZ fabric affecting ENI attachments; they are investigating. No ETA yet. They recommend limiting new connections to affected AZ.

ben (eng-runtime): New nodes are joining: 3/4 ready in us-west-3b. kvcache warming in progress: token-serving backpressure observed but rate limiter is holding. 5xx rate down to 3% now.

alice (oncall-sre): Good. I'll prepare a short incident note and handoff to daytime oncall in 45m. Key follow-ups: (1) collaborate with AWS on a permanent fix or AZ remediation (2) review autoscaler thresholds to avoid single-AZ exhaustion (3) postmortem with timeline + customer impact.

frank (pagerduty): Noting pager burn: 1 escalation, multiple re-pagers. Total page recipients: 6.

eve (prod-support): I'll include the list of affected tenants and the customer-impact summary. We may need to offer credits for sustained SLA violations if it crosses threshold.

david (oncall-eng): Handing off to alice-next (day-shift) in 45m. I'll remain available until then. Current state: routing override active, 4 fallback nodes (3 ready), cordoned 3 nodes in usw3a, AWS case open.

alice (oncall-sre): Handoff acknowledged. Next steps for day-shift: coordinate with netops on AWS case updates, monitor 5xx and kvcache, and plan traffic rebalancing once AWS declares AZ healthy. I'll update incident in #incidents-summary channel and attach timeline. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Thread closed for new automated alerts. Manual updates still allowed.
